text:
# A defect in the construct: the level-relation target is introduced by a distinction P9 does not actually make

I want to criticize the construct on one specific point, not to review it whole. The point is the move from "the P9 compatibility objection is closest in structure to P7's 'assumption that logical time is meaningful' but the assumption being questioned is different" to the claim that the objection has a target — the *level-relation target* — that P7's taxonomy does not list. I think this move depends on a distinction between "criticizing the interval" and "criticizing the independence assumption" that the construct reads into P9 rather than finds there. If that reading is right, the proposed addition to P7's taxonomy weakens, and the construct's own retreat clause ("If it is merely a re-description … my addition is not needed") becomes the more plausible outcome.

## What P9 says, and what it does with the word "invisible"

The construct's case rests heavily on this passage, quoted in the construct itself:

> "booking A's high alternative might be incompatible with booking B's high alternative if they share a physical resource not named in the snapshot. The snapshot does not name physical resources, so this incompatibility is invisible."

The construct reads "invisible" as marking a *conditional* premise: the incompatibility is not asserted to obtain, only that if it obtained, the interval would lose it. On that reading, the objection charges the interval with being an insufficient summary of a possibility that may or may not be real.

But notice what P9 actually does in the sentence immediately after, which the construct quotes in its P9 source but does not foreground:

> "A conjecture: the snapshot is under-specified for any real warehouse, and the best one can do is expose the unresolved alternatives rather than pretend to a single answer. A criticism: exposing alternatives without a policy for resolving them pushes the problem downstream, where it may be resolved badly or inconsistently."

So P9's own text already ships the objection *with a paired counter-criticism*, and it presents the exposure conclusion as "a conjecture," not a settled result. The construct correctly preserves the counter-criticism. But in doing so it also undercuts its own opening: if the objection's force in P9 is already a contested conjecture in the source, then P9 is not presenting the compatibility objection as a criticism that *needs a target of a new kind*. It is presenting it as one move in an argument in which both sides are already in view. That is a different shape from "here is a criticism whose target P7 forgot to name."

## The distinction the construct adds, stated precisely

The construct wants a target that is neither a rule, record, booking history, snapshot, nor assumption-about-time. It calls this a criticism of "the relationship between two levels" — of the assumption that per-booking sets are independently variable under aggregation. It then argues that one can accept the P9 objection while keeping the numeric interval, simply relabelling it "the range of availabilities *under the independence assumption*."

Here is the difficulty. Under P7's own wording, criticism targets include "the snapshot as a whole," and P7 explicitly names one assumption (logical time) as a candidate target. The construct claims the independence-assumption target is "closest to" the logical-time assumption "in structure" but is not that assumption. Grant the structural point for the sake of argument. The question the construct itself raises — is this "merely a re-description" of one of P7's existing entries? — has to be answered before the addition is warranted, and I do not think the construct supplies a reason it is not a re-description of "criticize the snapshot as a whole."

Consider what "criticize the snapshot as a whole" would have to mean if it is not to encompass the independence worry. P7 gives three illustrative meanings for "this snapshot is inconsistent": two active holds at a greatest revision, total reservations exceeding capacity, or logical time behind an expected expiry. The construct notes that the compatibility objection fits none of these and concludes that it is therefore not a criticism of "the snapshot as a whole." But P7 says "might mean," offering illustrations, not an exhaustive enumeration — and the construct itself notes P7's list "is not exhaustive by its own wording." If the snapshot-as-a-whole target is not exhausted by those three illustrations, then the compatibility worry may simply be another way of criticizing the snapshot as a whole, not a new target. The snapshot fails to name a resource that would decide cross-booking compatibility; that is a defect of the snapshot, attributable to the snapshot as a whole, in a way parallel to "the logical time is behind an expiry that someone expected to have passed" (which is also a defect of the snapshot as a whole, conditional on someone's expectation).

The construct's argument for a new target is that the rule "take the min/max per booking" can be accepted as correct while the objection still stands. True. But that only shows the objection does not target the *rule* — a point P7 already handles by giving rule, record, snapshot, etc. as separate options. It does not show the objection is not a snapshot-level criticism. And the construct's alternative framing — that the interval's *asserted meaning* changes while its *procedure* does not — is exactly what one would expect a snapshot-as-a-whole criticism to produce: a shift in what the snapshot's derived quantity is claimed to be, without altering the local computation.

## Why this is not merely a terminological quibble

If the level-relation target is actually a re-description of an existing target, two consequences follow that the construct does not acknowledge.

First, the construct's central answer to the operator question — "it requires a change to what the global-availability account is claimed to be, not necessarily to how it is computed" — becomes a claim *within* P7's existing taxonomy rather than a taxonomic extension. That is a substantive shift: the construct presents itself as adding a target P7 lacks, and the argument for the addition is what makes the reinterpretation of the global-availability account look like it is doing work beyond relabelling. Without the addition, "relabel the interval as conditional on independence" is just one more possible reassignment of a snapshot-level criticism to a narrower claim.

Second, the construct's "discriminating question" — whether the level-relation target offers anything the P7 taxonomy does not — has, on my reading, the answer "no, it does not." The construct treats that as an open possibility; I think the available text tilts toward it, because P7's list is offered as open-ended and because the snapshot-as-a-whole entry is broad enough to absorb the compatibility worry once we stop reading its three illustrations as exhaustive. This is a proposed defect, not one established from the packet; I cannot prove the construct is wrong from the frozen material alone, since P7's non-exhaustiveness is compatible with there being additional targets and the construct does not claim exhaustiveness either way.

## What the construct could have said to close the gap

To warrant the new target, the construct would need a case in which a snapshot-level criticism is *not available* under P7's own framing while the independence worry is available. The construct gestures at this ("not the snapshot as a whole in P7's listed senses") but grounds it only in the three illustrations, which P7 does not present as a closed list. An actual discriminating case would be one where the snapshot's own internal relations are all acceptable and no assumption about time is in question, yet the independence worry still bites — and where the construct shows why "criticize the snapshot as a whole" cannot cover that. It does not supply such a case; instead it supplies a case where the *rule* is not the target, which is already covered.

I want to be clear about the limits of this criticism. I am not claiming the level-relation framing is wrong or that no new target could be needed. I am claiming that the construct's own argument for the addition does not succeed on the text it supplies, and that the construct's own retreat clause names the outcome my reading favours. If someone can supply a case where the compatibility worry is not absorbable by "criticize the snapshot as a whole" and not reducible to "criticize the assumption that logical time is meaningful" or to the rule target, the addition stands. The construct does not do that, and its "discriminating question" leaves the matter open in the direction of non-addition.

## A separate note on the E009 record's role

The construct says the E009 record's "Non-convexity and cross-booking correlations" passage "gestures at the same locus without assigning it a target." That is fair as a description of the record, but the record's passage is also doing something the construct's framing obscures: it treats non-convexity and cross-booking correlation as *expressiveness limitations of WHL*, and proposes (without installing) a resource model or possible-worlds set. The construct's departure is therefore sharper than "the E009 record doesn't name the target either." The record's diagnosis is that WHL *cannot express* the correlation; the construct's proposal is that the existing account can be reinterpreted without language extension. These are different diagnoses of the same locus, and the construct's phrasing blurs that they are competing rather than complementary. Whether the record's expressiveness diagnosis or the construct's reinterpretation is the better response is unresolved, and the construct's "separate proposal, not an amendment" framing is correct on that point, but it should not be read as if the record's passage and the construct's target were two sides of the same observation. They are two readings of the same passage with different diagnoses; the packet does not settle between them.

I have not edited or replaced J; I have not endorsed any repair; and I have not settled the taxonomic question. The defect I am proposing is that the construct's argument for adding a target to P7's list does not survive its own retreat clause, on the text it quotes. The defect is proposed, not established, because P7's non-exhaustiveness and the construct's refusal to claim exhaustiveness leave room for the addition — room the construct does not close, but also does not need to close if some other case can be given.
